title: Brazil: show how power changes institutions

narration_and_visual_sequence.relationship: The decree changes the authority available to the presidency.
narration_and_visual_sequence.action: Move from the decree into a larger institutional view; activate one power relationship.

narration_and_visual_sequence.narration: Congress could be closed and rights restricted.
narration_and_visual_sequence.action: Close the Congress doors, then show the restriction on rights; retire each explanatory label after use.
narration_and_visual_sequence.hold: Hold each consequence long enough to inspect.

narration_and_visual_sequence.narration: The return to civilian government was gradual.
narration_and_visual_sequence.relationship: Contrast the earlier concentration of power with the later civilian transition.
narration_and_visual_sequence.action: Transform the established institutions across the timeline with a shared visual anchor.
narration_and_visual_sequence.hold: Hold the final contrast without implying all repression legacies vanished.

improvement_target: The source is a useful starting point, not the finish standard: institutional diagrams can remain unchanged while several claims are narrated. Enlarge one institution at a time, show doors closing and scrutiny changing through actual object states, strengthen human figures and material detail, and remove stale dates/arrows. Avoid reducing the lesson to badges, arrows and tiny icons.
adaptation: Borrow explanatory structure and object continuity. Selected STYLE.md governs artwork. Do not copy topic facts, timing or imperfections.
